03What It IsOVERVIEW▶

A Claude skill that packages an existing Autodesk Fusion add-in so anyone can install it by double-clicking a file, with no admin rights, no system changes and no extra software. The three installers sit inside the add-in folder; the whole folder is zipped and shared.

It has one file, its SKILL.md, which holds the installer and README templates, six rules that are not optional, notes on the executable bit, Gatekeeper, SmartScreen and the Windows execution policy, and a packaging checklist. The fusion-palette-addin skill uses it for every house-spec tool.

Why it mattersHand-copying into Fusion's hidden AddIns folder is where non-technical users give up. A double-click installer that wipes the old copy, skips caches and pauses to show the result makes every reinstall clean and repeatable.
04What It DoesOVERVIEW▶
  • macOS InstallerWrites install-macos.command: finds its own folder, checks Fusion's AddIns folder exists, deletes the old copy, copies the add-in with cp -R, removes the installers, .DS_Store and every __pycache__, then waits for Return.
  • Windows LauncherWrites install-windows.cmd, which only runs the PowerShell installer with -ExecutionPolicy Bypass for that one process, so nothing on the PC changes.
  • Windows InstallerWrites install-windows.ps1: checks %APPDATA%\Autodesk\Autodesk Fusion 360\API\AddIns exists, deletes the old copy, copies everything except the installers, removes every __pycache__ and .DS_Store (subfolders too), then waits for Enter.
  • READMEWrites a plain-text README.txt with the add-in's name and version, the install steps for macOS (Gatekeeper) and Windows (Extract All, SmartScreen), how to run it in Fusion, how to update it, and how to remove it. It travels with the zip, and the installers don't copy it into Fusion.
  • One NameSets ADDIN_NAME once at the top of each installer, matching the folder, the .py and the .manifest.
  • Executable ZipZips with the zip command, or with Python using a helper that sets the executable bit, then confirms it with unzip -Z.
  • Closing MessageEnds both installers with the same closing message: where to find the add-in in Fusion, plus anything true of this add-in (where its button lands, that the listed version updates after a restart, what survives reinstalls). The handoff also tells Windows users to Extract All first and how to get past SmartScreen.
  • ChecklistChecks the names match, the .command is executable in the zip, README.txt is there with the Gatekeeper and Windows steps, no caches, .pyc or zero-byte files are in it, and the manifest version matches the add-in's.

08Capabilities and LimitationsSCOPE▶
  • Both PlatformsOne zip installs on macOS and Windows, with the same message on both.
  • Clean ReinstallEach run wipes the old copy first, so renamed or deleted files from an older version can't linger.
  • No Admin RightsCopies into per-user folders and changes no system setting, including the PowerShell execution policy.
  • Works AnywhereEach script finds its own folder, so it works wherever the zip is unpacked.
  • Clear FailureIf Fusion's AddIns folder is missing it says so and stops, instead of creating folders in the wrong place.
  • Not SignedPlain scripts, not signed or notarized packages: Gatekeeper asks once on a Mac, and SmartScreen may ask on Windows.
  • Doesn't Start ItIt installs but doesn't run the add-in; you click Run in Scripts and Add-Ins once (after that, runOnStartup loads it).
  • Fusion OnlyNot for other software, and not for MSI, PKG or notarized installers.
  • Not the Add-in ItselfIt doesn't write the add-in's code or UI; that's fusion-addin-scaffold or fusion-palette-addin.
  • No UninstallerThere is no uninstall script; the README says how to remove an add-in (stop it in Fusion and delete its folder from AddIns).

11GotchasGOTCHAS▶
  • Names Must MatchThe folder, .py, .manifest and ADDIN_NAME must all be the same, or Fusion won't list the add-in.
  • Lost Executable BitPython's zipfile saves the .command without the executable bit, so double-clicking does nothing. Use the zip command or the helper; recovery is chmod +x install-macos.command.
  • Stale CachesOld Python cache folders (__pycache__) or .pyc files from another Python version can stop an add-in loading with no useful error; the installers skip them, along with Finder's .DS_Store files.
  • Copying Over the TopCopying onto an old install leaves orphaned files, so a renamed module keeps working from its old copy. The installers delete the old folder first.
  • Self-nestingInstallers that copy themselves nest another copy on each reinstall; these exclude themselves.
  • GatekeepermacOS puts downloaded files in quarantine, so the first double-click may say "unidentified developer": right-click › Open › Open, once. Never disable Gatekeeper.
  • Blocked Before It RunsGatekeeper and SmartScreen stop the installer before it can show any message, so the way past them has to be written outside it, in README.txt.
  • Fusion 360 in the PathThe folder is still called "Autodesk Fusion 360" even though the product is now just Fusion.
  • Version After RestartThe version shown in Scripts and Add-Ins is read when Fusion starts, so it may lag until a restart.
  • Empty FilesA truncated write leaves a zero-byte file, and py_compile passes on it; the checklist checks every file's size.
  • Windows: Extract FirstRun the installer from an extracted folder, not from inside the zip. If SmartScreen appears, More info › Run anyway. The handoff message covers both.
  • Windows: .cmd, Not .ps1Double-click the .cmd. Never run Set-ExecutionPolicy; the .cmd bypasses the policy for one run only.
  • Caches in SubfoldersA __pycache__ can sit in a subfolder of the add-in, not just at the top. Both installers now remove it everywhere after copying (the PowerShell one gained this on Nov 9, 2026).
12Other RequirementsREFERENCE▶
  • FusionAutodesk Fusion installed and set up for the current user on macOS, or on Windows 10 or 11.
  • An Add-inAn existing add-in folder whose .py and .manifest share the folder's name.
  • Code ExecutionClaude needs code execution ("Create and edit files") to zip with the executable bit and run the checklist.
  • No Admin RightsNothing needs an administrator password on either platform.

TermTopicDefinitionAppears inQty
Add-inFusionA Python program Fusion loads from its AddIns folder; it can start with Fusion and add buttons.
AddIns folderFusionThe per-user folder Fusion loads add-ins from, still under "Autodesk Fusion 360" on both platforms.
ManifestFusionThe JSON file next to the .py that tells Fusion the add-in's id, version and platforms.
ADDIN_NAMEInstallerThe one variable at the top of each installer that names the add-in folder to install.
.command fileInstallerA shell script macOS opens in Terminal when you double-click it.
LauncherInstallerThe .cmd file whose only job is to start the PowerShell installer.
Closing messageInstallerThe lines both installers print after "Done": how to run the add-in and anything true of it.
Executable bitPackagingThe file permission that lets a .command run on double-click; Python's zipfile drops it.
__pycache__PackagingPython's compiled-file cache; a stale copy from another Python version can stop an add-in loading.
.DS_StorePackagingA hidden Finder settings file macOS adds to folders; the installers skip it.
Zero-byte filePackagingAn empty file left by a truncated write; the checklist rejects it.
GatekeeperSecuritymacOS protection that blocks unsigned downloaded files until you right-click › Open once.
QuarantineSecurityThe mark macOS puts on downloaded files, which triggers Gatekeeper.
SmartScreenSecurityWindows protection that may warn before running a downloaded file; More info › Run anyway.
Execution policySecurityThe PowerShell setting that blocks .ps1 files; the .cmd bypasses it for one process only.
NotarizedSecuritySigned and checked by Apple; these installers are not, which is why Gatekeeper asks.
README.txtInstallerThe plain-text install guide in the zip, for whoever receives it; the installers don't copy it into Fusion.
